caption:
I ranked 6 ways employees pay less tax, legally. General info, 2026–27 rules.

S: Salary sacrifice into super. Contributions are taxed at 15% in the fund instead of your marginal rate. The catch: the $32,500 cap includes your employer's super, and the money is locked away until you retire.

A: Carry-forward contributions. Unused cap from up to 5 previous years, if your total super balance was under $500,000 at 30 June last year.

A: Itemising. If your real work costs are more than $1,000, claim them with records.

B: The $1,000 standard deduction. Automatic and receipt-free, but it's the floor, not a strategy.

C: Private hospital cover. Singles over $105,000 without it pay a Medicare levy surcharge of 1% to 1.5%. Whether cover costs less than the surcharge depends on you.

D: Buying things "for the deduction". You spend a dollar to get about 30 cents back.

The ranking is a general view of how much each can move a typical employee's bill. Yours depends on your income, age and cash flow.

Agree with the order?

#paylesslegally #australiantax #salarysacrifice #superannuation #taxtips
figures_checked: Salary-sacrificed super taxed at 15% in the fund; Division 293 above $250,000 (ATO Salary sacrificing super, checked 11 Nov 2026; Div 293 threshold re-confirmed 15 Nov 2026)
Concessional contributions cap $32,500 for 2026–27 (ATO Key super rates and thresholds, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Carry-forward concessional contributions: total super balance under $500,000 at 30 June of the previous year, unused cap from up to 5 previous years (ATO Caps, limits and tax on super contributions, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Standard deduction up to $1,000 from 2026–27, automatic, residents with labour income, no records; actual work claims reduce it; $300 work-expense and $150 laundry no-receipt exceptions end 1 July 2026; union fees, donations, tax agent fees, income protection premiums, personal super contributions, investment/rental deductions claimable on top (ATO Standard deduction for work-related expenses, updated 2 Nov 2026, checked 15 Nov 2026)
Medicare levy surcharge 2026–27: singles over $105,000, families over $210,000; 1% / 1.25% / 1.5% tiers (ATO Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Resident rates 2026–27: nil to $18,200; 15c to $45,000; $4,020 + 30c to $135,000; $31,020 + 37c to $190,000; $51,370 + 45c above; Medicare levy 2% not included (ATO Tax rates – Australian residents, checked 15 Nov 2026)
